options.method: wpr records the providers below, under the instance name, to a file inside the bundle for the window; PresentMon then reads that file with --etl_file and prints its CSV on stdout, captured under the artifact cap; the file is deleted after it was read because a WPR merged recording may carry the network adapter hardware and IP addresses. Live PresentMon is not run: in realtime mode it opens a PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION handle to every presenting process (OutputThread.cpp QueryProcessName, v2.6.0) and enables SeDebugPrivilege when it can (MainThread.cpp); with --etl_file both are skipped (the same two functions test args.mEtlFileName)

providers.source: EnableProvidersListing: ProcessStart_Start, ProcessStop_Stop, ProcessRundown_Info, plus EVENT_CONTROL_CODE_CAPTURE_STATE for the rundown of processes already running

EnableProvidersListing: the present history, flip, blit, queue packet, VSync, context, device, hardware queue and DMA packet events for track display and track GPU; the Performance keyword (0x4000000000000000) is removed as PresentMon does; capture state for Context_DCStart and Device_DCStart
EnableProvidersListing: TokenCompositionSurfaceObject_Info, TokenStateChanged_Info (track display), InputDeviceRead_Stop, RetrieveInputMessage_Info, OnInputXformUpdate_Info (track input)

EnableProvidersListing: GetPresentHistory_Info, SCHEDULE_PRESENT_Start, SCHEDULE_SURFACEUPDATE_Info, FlipChain_Pending, FlipChain_Complete, FlipChain_Dirty; Composition (0x1) is added for Windows 10, where PresentMon swaps it for Scheduling (0x80)

options.output_paths_recorded_as: bundle relative paths; the processes received the absolute paths of the same files in this bundle, in double quotes
options.recording_deleted_because: a WPR merged recording may hold the network adapter hardware and IP addresses (SystemConfig_NIC through the merge's NetworkInterface custom event); the project keeps those out of every bundle, so the recording is read on the PC and deleted. recording.json keeps its size, SHA-256 and header

disk_budget.note: the session stops at session_file_max_bytes (MaximumFileSize, sequential); the merged file is checked against merged_file_max_bytes and deleted either way; the CSV is captured under csv_max_bytes by the process runner, which stops PresentMon at the cap; the merge temp folder is removed on every path. The peak is bounded by the session file plus the merged file plus the CSV plus two console streams (peak_bytes_bound), and ETW keeps 200 MB free on the system drive

option_citations.--etl_file: Analyze an ETW trace log file instead of the actively running processes.
option_citations.--qpc_time: Output the CPU start time as a performance counter value.
option_citations.--process_name: Only record processes with the specified exe name. This argument can be repeated to capture multiple processes.
option_citations.wpr -start: Starts one or more profiles. -filemode: recording is done in file mode. -recordtempto: the temporary folder path that the recording is saved to.
option_citations.wpr -status: Displays the status of an active recording (if any). collectors: lists collector information, with Events Lost per collector and the enabled providers.
option_citations.wpr -stop: Cancels and saves the recording initiated by WPR (if any) to the given file. -skipPdbGen disables dynamic generation of pdbs for .NET modules.
option_citations.wpr -cancel: Cancels the current recording without saving the recorded data.
option_citations.-instancename: Specifies a name to uniquely identify the tracing instance. This option can be applied to any commands that manipulate the logging session. -instancename must be the last parameter.

calibration.method: one thread reads Stopwatch.GetTimestamp (QueryPerformanceCounter), [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToFileTimeUtc() (the system time at the resolution of the system timer), Stopwatch.GetTimestamp, at the session start, every 5 s strictly inside the session, and at the stop. Each pair is taken at the instant the system clock changes value: the clock is read in a loop until it changes, and the counter read before the last unchanged reading and the one after the changed reading bracket the moment the clock took its new value; the size of that change (the clock increment) is recorded with the pair. The frequency is Stopwatch.Frequency (QueryPerformanceFrequency). GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime and GetSystemTimeAdjustment are not called: neither is reachable from Windows PowerShell 5.1 without compiling code, so both members of time_adjustment are null. See docs/clock-calibration.md.

notes: Scenario runner 1.0.0, scenario s1 version 1.0.0: One bounded latency session on the gaming PC: the state before, the DPC and interrupt trace and the frame recording inside one clock calibration session, the history collectors, and the state after.
Ran as the collector account (its name is not recorded); elevated: True; member of Event Log Readers (S-1-5-32-573): True; member of Performance Log Users (S-1-5-32-559): False.

Each collector ran as its own Windows PowerShell process, one after another, except the clock session, which ran in the background across the live captures. Each collector's own manifest, summary and log are kept under logs/steps/<step>/ with the profile folder written as <profile>, the account as <account> and this directory as <bundle>; raw/ holds every source the runner merged, under its own id or with the step's prefix (state_before_, state_after_).
In this scenario the history steps are optional: their sources are listed with required false whatever the collector marked.
